jmpost repository guide

Source: AGENTS.md

Purpose

jmpost is an R package for Bayesian joint models that combine:

  • a parametric time-to-event (survival) submodel;
  • a linear or nonlinear mixed-effects longitudinal submodel for a continuous marker, primarily tumour-size trajectories; and
  • one or more association/link terms connecting the longitudinal trajectory to survival.

The R layer builds data and model specifications, renders a complete Stan program, compiles it with cmdstanr, samples it, and provides posterior quantities, simulation, scoring, and plotting helpers. The package requires R >= 4.1 and is not yet on CRAN.

Repository map

  • R/: package implementation. Most domain objects are S4 classes with public constructors plus S3 methods/generics.
  • inst/stan/base/: shared Stan templates and functions used to assemble a joint model.
  • inst/stan/lm-*/: built-in longitudinal-model modules. Directories ending in -cov are covariate-enabled variants.
  • inst/stan/sm-*/: built-in parametric survival-model modules.
  • tests/testthat/: testthat edition 3 tests, generally named after the R class or feature under test. tests/testthat/models/ contains Stan fixtures.
  • vignettes/: Quarto user guides and custom-model Stan examples.
  • data/ and R/data.R: packaged example datasets and their documentation.
  • data-raw/: source files and scripts used to create packaged data.
  • man/ and NAMESPACE: generated by roxygen2; do not edit by hand.
  • README.Rmd: source for generated README.md; edit the Rmd, then regenerate.
  • design/: exploratory, design, debugging, and legacy material; it is excluded from package builds and from Air formatting.
  • .github/workflows/: reusable CI workflows for checks, coverage, docs, linting, spelling, links, dependency audit, and releases.

Main object and execution flow

  1. DataSubject, DataSurvival, and DataLongitudinal validate and harmonise user data; DataJoint combines them and converts them to Stan data.
  2. A longitudinal model (LongitudinalGSF, LongitudinalSteinFojo, LongitudinalClaretBruno, LongitudinalRandomSlope, and covariate variants), a survival model (SurvivalExponential, SurvivalGamma, SurvivalLoglogistic, or SurvivalWeibullPH), and Link components are composed by JointModel.
  3. Parameter, Prior, and ParameterList define declarations, priors, and initial values. Promise objects defer link/model details until composition.
  4. StanModule parses and merges Stan blocks. as.StanModule.JointModel() renders inst/stan/base/base.stan with jinjar and combines component modules. compileStanModel() caches compiled executables by a digest of the generated Stan code.
  5. sampleStanModel() returns JointModelSamples. Quantity generators and grid classes drive generated quantities for subject, population, and prediction use cases.

When changing a model, inspect both its R/<Model>.R implementation and the matching inst/stan/<model>/ directory. Changes to shared rendering or data contracts can affect every model, so include focused rendering/data tests as well as the model-specific test.

Development conventions

  • Follow the existing four-space R style. air.toml sets an 80-column line width and excludes design/; format R code with air format <paths> when Air is available.
  • Preserve the package’s British English spelling (Language: en-GB). Add intentional specialist terms to inst/WORDLIST if spelling CI requires it.
  • Public APIs and S3 methods are documented with roxygen comments in R/. This project also uses roxytypes typed tags such as @typed.
  • Regenerate documentation after changing exports, signatures, classes, or roxygen text; never patch NAMESPACE or man/*.Rd directly.
  • DESCRIPTION has an explicit Collate order. New R files may need to be placed there according to their class/generic dependencies; existing files also use roxygen @include declarations.
  • Keep R-side names, dimensions, and declarations synchronized with Stan-side templates. Prefer composing StanModules over duplicating shared Stan code.
  • Use read_stan() for packaged Stan fragments and decorated_render() for Jinja-style templating, consistent with existing modules.
  • Add regression tests in the closest matching test-*.R file. Use a small dedicated fixture under tests/testthat/models/ only when the Stan source is itself part of the behavior under test.
  • Do not commit compiled Stan executables, generated CmdStan source, R check directories, rendered vignettes, or local caches.

Testing and validation

Use the narrowest useful check first, then broaden it in proportion to the change. Typical commands from the repository root are:

Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all(helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE); testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-<feature>.R")'
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'

Notes:

  • Tests run with testthat edition 3 and parallel testing enabled.
  • Stan compilation/sampling requires cmdstanr plus a working CmdStan install. R/zzz.R recognizes CMDSTAN and CMDSTAN_PATH.
  • Set JMPOST_CACHE_DIR to reuse compiled Stan models across runs. Otherwise a session-specific temporary directory is used.
  • Many expensive comparison, compilation, and sampling tests are guarded by JMPOST_FULL_TEST=TRUE; routine local tests intentionally skip those cases.
  • Visual snapshot updates/checks are controlled by JMPOST_GRAPH_SNAPSHOT=TRUE.
  • CI uses NOT_CRAN=TRUE and CmdStan environment variables. The scheduled workflow enables both full tests and graph snapshots.
  • For Stan-template changes, useful focused coverage includes test-StanModel.R, test-StanModule.R, test-jinjar_render.R, test-stan_functions.R, and the affected model’s test file.

Documentation and examples

  • The quickest package overview and end-to-end example is in README.Rmd.
  • vignettes/quickstart.qmd covers normal fitting; statistical-specification.qmd explains the model; extending-jmpost.qmd and the custom-model vignettes cover extension points.
  • Keep examples lightweight. Sampling or compilation examples that are not appropriate for routine checks should remain guarded (for example with \dontrun{} in roxygen examples).
  • Pkgdown configuration lives in _pkgdown.yml; Quarto is the vignette builder.

Code reviews

For every requested code review or pull-request review, load and follow the repository’s critical-code-reviewer skill before inspecting the change. Use that skill’s severity, evidence, testing, and reporting guidance, and prioritize correctness, statistical/Stan behavior, security, accessibility where relevant, maintainability, tests, and edge cases.

During review, pay particular attention to R/Stan contract mismatches, incorrect parameter constraints or dimensions, numerical stability, generated-quantity behavior, class validity, optional survival-only or longitudinal-only models, and whether expensive paths have an appropriate test strategy.
